t: This is Our Lady of the Assumption and St Gregory, a Catholic church on Warwick Street. It's the oldest Catholic church in England, and the only surviving eighteenth-century Catholic chapel in London. It began as the Royal Bavarian Chapel, a chapel within a foreign embassy. It was built between 1789 and 1790 to designs by Joseph Bonomi the Elder, an Italian architect who spent most of his career in England and was Robert Adam's leading draughtsman. Today it's the central church of the Personal Ordinariate of Our Lady of Walsingham.
